qcd_compiler_rule.carrier: positive Q(√-10) / su(5)-adjoint sector gives k3_bare=24/Phi3
qcd_compiler_rule.threshold: negative Q(√-7) / so(6)-adjoint sector gives tau=log sqrt(mu/Phi6)

theorem_statement: The 78-dimensional Hashimoto/Ramanujan shell is an E6-sized two-adjoint compiler: its complex multiplicities 24 and 15 are exactly dim su(5) and dim so(6)=dim su(4).  The selected QCD coupling uses the su(5)-sized positive sector as the bare carrier and the so(6)/Phi6 negative sector as the heavy threshold.
interpretive_note: This explains why the successful alpha_s formula uses 24/13 and a Phi6 polar threshold.  The number 24 is not merely convenient; it is the positive Hashimoto multiplicity and the SU(5) adjoint dimension.  The number 15 is not passive; it is the negative Hashimoto multiplicity and the SO(6)/SU(4) adjoint dimension that carries the Phi6 threshold.
